<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par152 />afterwards); thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=62|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי}} is evidently to be supplied, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=10}} the corresponding jussive from the preceding imperatives, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=12}} from the preceding infinitive absolute.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|h}}
2. {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}}, like {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}, regularly stands immediately before the verb, but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=6|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=2|hidebook=1}} before another strongly emphasized member of the sentence.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=3}} the pointing {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} occurs twice instead of {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}}, and is thus, in the opinion of the Masoretes, equivalent to ''against'' him that ''bendeth''; but undoubtedly we should read {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|i}}
(''c'') {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} construct state (unless it be sometimes merely a contracted connective form, cf. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵים}} for {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַ֫יִם}} {{GHGpar|97|d}}) of {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫יִן|translate=non-existence}} (as also the absolute state, see below) is the negative of {{GHGheb|text=יֵשׁ|translate=existence}}; cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=29}} with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=5|verse=5}}. As {{GHGheb|text=יֵשׁ}} (''he, she, it is, was'', &c.) includes the idea of ''being'' in all tenses, so {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫יִן}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} includes the idea of ''not being'' in all tenses. Hence—

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|k}}
(1) The absolute state {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫יִן}}, with an evident transition to the meaning of a verbal predicate, ''there does not exist'', always ''follows'' the word negatived, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=3}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=3}}) {{GHGheb|text=וְכֹחַ אַ֫יִן לְלֵדָה|translate=and strength does not exist to bring forth}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫יִן|translate=was not}} present; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=אִם־אָֽיִן|translate=or is he not}}? after {{GHGheb|text=הֲיֵשׁ|translate=is he...}}? (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=20}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=37}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=20}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָֽיִן|translate=no}}). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=4}} and 10:14 {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫יִן}} is used in reference to a plural; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=וָאַ֫יִן|translate=and let there be none, let none come!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=19}}.—Cf. finally {{GHGheb|text=אִם־אַ֫יִן|translate=if it be not so}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=10}}.—Quite anomalous is {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫יִן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=35|verse=15}} before a perfect as an emphatic negation; the text, however, can hardly be correct.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|l}}
(2) The construct state {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} stands in its natural position immediately before the substantive whose non-existence it predicates, or before the subject of the sentence which is to be negatived. To the former class belong also the very numerous instances in which {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} is joined to a participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵין רֹאֶה וְאֵין יוֹדֵעַ וְאֵין מֵקִיץ|translate=and there was not one seeing}}, &c., i.e. ''and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither did any awake''; so especially {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵין}} with a participle in subordinate ''circumstantial'' or ''descriptive clauses'', such as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=29}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיַפְלִיט וְאֵין מַצִּיל|translate=and he shall carry it away}}, while there is none delivering, i.e. ''without any one’s delivering'' it; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=3}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=6}} &c., {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵין מַֽחֲרִיד}} ''without any one’s making you afraid''; cf. {{GHGpar|141|e}}. {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} is used as the negation of an entire noun-clause, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=42}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵין יְהוַֹה בִּקִרְבְּכֶם|translate=the Lord is not among you}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=29}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽין־יוֹסֵף בַּבּוֹר|translate=Joseph was not in the pit}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|m}}
(3) When the subject which is to be negatived is a personal pronoun, it is joined as a suffix to {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}}, according to {{GHGpar|100|o}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֶ֫נִּי|translate=I am not, was not, shall not be}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽינְךָ}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֵךְ}}, ''thou art not'', &c.; {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֶ֫נּוּ}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֶ֫נָּה|translate=he, she is not}}, &c.; also absolutely, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=13}} ''he is'' (5:24 ''he was'') ''no'' longer ''alive''; {{GHGheb|text=אֵינָם|translate=they are not}}, &c. When the accompanying predicate is a verb, it follows again (see l) in the form of a participle, since {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} always introduces a noun-clause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֶ֫נִּי נׄתֵן|translate=I will not give}}; 8:17, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=32}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|n}}
Rem. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵין אֲנִי}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֶ֫נִּי}} is due to its being co-ordinate with three other (substantival) subjects; these are again expressly summed up in {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽין־אֲנַחְנוּ}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵין אֶתְכֶם}} the pronominal complement of {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} appears<section end=par152 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
